## Problem

A late LLM-review event for an old patchset can dispatch Gerrit Verified for that stale revision. Because Verified concurrency is keyed by change, the stale run supersedes and cancels useful work for the current patchset. This wastes scarce runners and can leave the current patchset without a complete CI verdict.

## Experimentally verified evidence

On Gerrit change 2225, current patchset 6 canonical Verified run 32926871119 started at 2026-08-26T03:33:08Z. The review bot finished and published an LLM-Review result for old patchset 5 at 03:43:46Z. GitHub run 32927544184 was created at 03:43:48Z; its completed ticket-validation job records `gerrit-refspec: refs/changes/25/2225/5`, proving it targets stale patchset 5. Run 32926871119 then reported `Canceling since a higher priority waiting request for gerrit-verify-rebar~2225 exists`; its mutation shard was canceled after 8m45s and its still-running Linux jobs were canceled.

Correction to the initial observation: four other runs created around 03:42:48-03:42:54 belong to other Gerrit changes (for example, run 32927478228 records `refs/changes/26/2226/3`). They are not duplicates for change 2225 and are excluded from this bug. The verified defect is one stale-PS5 run superseding the active PS6 run.

Related precedent `musophobic-secondary-jaguar` fixed the narrower `recheck-review` ChatOps word collision. This occurrence involves a late ordinary review result for a non-current revision and is therefore a distinct revision-filter/concurrency defect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A late review result for a non-current patchset does not dispatch Verified for that stale revision.
- [x] A stale-patchset event cannot supersede or cancel the current patchset's Verified run.
- [x] A new current patchset still dispatches exactly one canonical Verified run.
- [x] The authorized CI recheck mechanism for the current patchset still dispatches exactly one replacement run.
- [x] Tests replay PS5 review completion while PS6 CI is active and assert that PS6 remains active and no PS5 Verified dispatch occurs.
- [x] Diagnostics record the event revision, current revision, event type, and accepted/suppressed disposition without adding material runtime work.

## Acceptance-criteria evidence (Phase 2 — landed)

Fix landed as Gerrit change 2330, merged commit `afe01efaa8b2c685b5a44d527e1219e9d7a0ce59`
(`LLM-Review +1` PASS, `Verified +1` SUCCESS). Held-out RED->GREEN oracle:
`tests/unit/test_review_bot_stale_vote_baa8.py`.

- AC1/AC2 (no stale dispatch / no supersede-cancel): `_review_and_vote` now re-reads the
  change's current revision immediately before `post_review` and SUPPRESSES the vote when the
  reviewed revision is no longer current — so no Gerrit comment is posted on the stale
  revision, the `recheck=verify` g2p mapping never fires for it, and the current patchset's
  Verified run is never cancelled. Proven by `test_no_vote_when_revision_superseded_during_review`
  (RED on `main`, GREEN after fix; mutation-checked: defeating the guard re-reddens it).
- AC3 (a new current patchset still dispatches exactly one canonical Verified run): the
  patchset-created dispatch path (`.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`, g2p config) is
  UNCHANGED; the still-current control `test_votes_when_revision_still_current` confirms a
  current revision votes exactly as before.
- AC4 (authorized recheck still dispatches one replacement run): the `force`/`manual-rerun`
  path bypasses the new check (built FROM the current revision by construction) and votes
  normally — `test_forced_rerun_bypasses_staleness_and_votes`; the `recheck=verify` mapping is
  untouched.
- AC5 (replay PS5-completes-while-PS6-active): the oracle is the unit-boundary replay — it
  drives the real `voter.review_and_vote` with current-revision `rev2` != reviewed `rev1`
  (the PS5-review-completes-under-current-PS6 shape) and asserts NO vote is cast on `rev1`, so
  no stale Verified is dispatched and the current run is left active.
- AC6 (diagnostics, no material runtime work): on suppression `_superseded_before_vote` emits a
  single structured `voter_skip` record carrying `revision_id` (event/reviewed), `current_revision_id`,
  `event_type`, and `disposition=vote_suppressed_superseded` — one already-cheap REST lookup
  plus one log line.
- Fail-open safety: `test_fails_open_and_votes_when_current_revision_unknown` and
  `..._lookup_raises` confirm a Gerrit blip never drops a real review.
